prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Green Party Manifesto 2005 — Summary (under 500 words)

Vision: Build a sustainable, fair society by prioritising social, economic and environmental justice; restore trust in public services; tackle climate change; promote peace, equity and localisation.

Economy
- Tackle inequality via progressive income tax bands (50% over £50k; 60% over £100k) and a more banded Corporation Tax (up to 40% for biggest firms).
- Shift taxation from labour and consumption to resource use: phase out VAT, expand eco-taxes; abolish National Insurance and fund services via taxes on all income.
- Pilot a Land Value Tax to replace Council Tax and Uniform Business Rates; address concentrated land ownership.
- Support local economies: community banks, credit unions, local currencies; oppose UK entry to the euro; reform WTO rules; favour SMEs and co-ops.
- Replace GDP with wellbeing indicators (e.g., ISEW/MDP).

Energy and Climate
- Adopt Contraction and Convergence: cut UK CO2 by 20% (2010), 50% (2020), 85% (2030), towards 90% (2050); expand carbon trading.
- Introduce a Carbon Tax (replace 5% VAT on domestic energy and Climate Change Levy), with protections for low users.
- 40% of energy from renewables by 2020; major investment in solar, wind (on/offshore), wave, and biogas; create c. 200,000 jobs.
- Reduce demand via a Warmer Homes Act (30% domestic cut in 10 years) and council-led 45% emissions cuts by 2020.
- End nuclear power as stations reach end of life; shift R&D subsidies to renewables; create a cabinet role for climate policy.

Welfare
- Phase in a universal, non-withdrawable Citizen’s Income; retain and integrate housing/disability support appropriately.
- Citizen’s Pension: universal, earnings-linked, replacing Pension Credit; raises basic pension to c. £109 single/£167 couple (2005).
- Simplify child support; boost Child Benefit; reduce working hours (end 48-hour opt-out; explore 35-hour week); expand Sure Start.
- Boost affordable housing: allow councils to build, support co-ops, improve efficiency, reform land use.

Health and Education
- Restore NHS principles; end marketisation, PPPs, foundation hospitals; oppose GATS in public services.
- Abolish prescription charges; restore free eye tests and dental care; expand prevention and mental health; fund NHS to at least 9% of GNP (c. £90bn by 2008) with a dedicated NHS Tax.
- Increase education funding, especially early years/post-16; scrap tuition fees; restore maintenance grants; abolish SATs; move to Individual Learning Plans.

Transport
- Cut road traffic 10% by 2010; shift £30bn from roads to public transport; re-regulate buses.
- Return rail and Tube (track and operations) to public ownership; expand rail, freight, and light rail.
- Price true motoring costs: expand congestion/road pricing; raise fuel duty; incentivise efficient vehicles; fund R&D.
- Restrain aviation growth: no new runways, ban night flights, tax aviation fuel EU-wide, raise APD, tax domestic flight emissions.

Environment
- Zero Waste Strategy: legislate to reduce packaging, ban incineration, set recycled content standards; recycle 60% domestic waste by 2010; create a Zero Waste Agency.
- New eco-taxes and a national Environmental Protection Commission; strengthen chemicals regulation.
- Protect biodiversity and animal rights; apply the precautionary principle to GM, xenotransplantation, nanotech; end patents on natural genetic resources; ban live exports, battery cages (incl. enriched), fur imports; replace vivisection.

Food and Farming
- Organics Target Bill: 30% organic production by 2012; support local markets, co-ops, box schemes.
- Replace CAP/CFP with policies for localisation, biodiversity, and sustainable incomes; ban GM food.
- Toughen supermarkets’ Code of Practice; stronger OFT scrutiny.

Crime and Justice
- Prevent crime via better urban design, youth facilities, rapid repairs, visible staffing; treat drugs as a health issue; scrap ID cards.
- Strengthen community policing, accountability, and independent complaints; restore social “eyes and ears.”
- Tighten gun laws; single robust licensing; broad prohibitions; address gun culture.
- Expand restorative justice; protect human rights; tackle hate crimes and violence against women; stronger disability rights.

Democracy
- Oppose national ID cards; renew and empower local government (including LVT, recall, referenda).
- Proportional representation for councils and Westminster; elected House of Lords; devolved regional government by region; more powers for Scotland/Wales if desired.
- Draft a written constitution; disestablish Church of England.

International and Peace
- Ethical foreign policy: withdraw from Iraq, support UN peacekeeping, reduce defence to EU average, decommission nuclear weapons, end arms export subsidies; pursue an Arms Trade Treaty.
- Aid to 1% of GNI by 2010; cancel debts of 52 poorest countries; consider Tobin tax; reform UN (end permanent UNSC seats), IMF, World Bank.
- Reform WTO or replace with a General Agreement on Sustainable Trade to enable localisation, fair trade and environmental standards.
- Oppose proposed EU constitution; uphold asylum rights; enable work, fair benefits, independent appeals; ratify migrant workers’ rights convention.
